'''Simfit''' is a free [[open-source software|open-source]] [[Microsoft Windows|Windows]] package for simulation, curve fitting, statistics, and [https://simfit.uk/simfit.html plotting], using a library of models or user-defined mathematical [https://simfit.uk/user_defined_models.html equations]. Simfit has been developed by Bill Bardsley of the [[University of Manchester]].<ref name="Burguillo2003" /> Although it is written for Windows, it can easily be installed and used on Linux machines via [[Wine (software)|WINE]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=WineHQ - Simfit|url=https://appdb.winehq.org/objectManager.php?sClass=application&iId=5181|access-date=2021-10-04|website=appdb.winehq.org}}</ref>

Simfit is developed using [http://www.silverfrost.com Silverfrost Limited's] [[Silverfrost FTN95|FTN95]] Fortran Compiler and is currently featured on their website as a [http://www.silverfrost.com/37/ftn95/ftn95_showcase.aspx showcased application]. The graphical functionality in Simfit has been released as a Fortran library called [https://simfit.uk/simdem.html Simdem] which allows the programmer to produce charts and graphs with just a few lines of Fortran. A version of Simdem is shipped with the Windows version of the NAG Fortran Builder.<ref name="ACM2007" />

A Spanish-language version of Simfit is maintained by a team in [[Salamanca]].

At Version 8.1.1 a simplified version of simfit called sv_simfit designed for first-time users is bundled with the main simfit package.
